items.title: Iran says no new talks until framework agreed

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Iranian official talks nuclear program with CNN

items.description:
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh on Saturday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims about enriched uranium, declaring that Tehran will not hand over its stockpiles to the United States and that no date has been set for a new round of negotiations. Speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomatic Forum in Turkey, Khatibzadeh said the Iranians were not ready for face-to-face talks because the American negotiating position had not changed.[1][2][3]

"Until we agree on the framework, we cannot set the date," Khatibzadeh told reporters, according to Reuters. His remarks came days after Trump said on April 16 that the United States was "very close" to a deal and that Iran had "agreed to almost everything," including handing over its enriched uranium stockpile.[4][1]

items.title: The quiet disappearance of Australia's rainfall observation network
items.description: For more than 60 years, Frank Pritchard has diligently checked the weather, adding to a record that stretches back more than a century. But he's part of a quietly shrinking network of observers around Australia. Without it, scientists say we risk missing out on important information that could help improve weather forecast models and climate projections.

items.title: Egypt, Pakistan building framework for lasting US-Iran peace

featured_image.name: Saudi, Pakistani, Egyptian FMs to join Türkiye talks at ...

items.description:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed on Saturday that Egypt and Pakistan are working closely together on a framework to secure a lasting peace between the United States and Iran, as four regional powers intensify diplomacy ahead of a ceasefire deadline set to expire on April 22.[1]

Abdelatty said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating on a broader regional initiative aimed at preventing further escalation and building a post-conflict security arrangement. He stressed the need to protect Gulf nations and ensure the stability of energy markets, supply chains, and food security.[1]

items.title: Iranians face 50th day of internet blackout as ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Ceasefire brings some relief for Iranians but economic outlook ...

items.description: As a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran inches toward its April 22 expiration, Iranians are navigating a precarious existence shaped by weeks of aerial bombardment, a brutal government crackdown on mass protests, and an economic crisis with no clear end in sight. The pause in fighting has brought a measure of relief — but for many, it has also sharpened fears that the worst may still lie ahead.

items.title: Iranians fear regime will tighten grip once ceasefire holds

featured_image.name: Military Parade Of Iran's SelfSacrificing Daughters

items.description:
Iranians struggling to piece together daily life after weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes and a brutal crackdown on protesters are gripped by fear that conditions will only worsen once the guns fall silent, even as a fragile ceasefire offers a momentary reprieve.

"The war will end, but that's when our real problems with the system begin," a 37-year-old named Fariba who took part in the January unrest told Reuters by phone from Iran. "I'm very afraid that if the regime reaches an agreement with the United States, it will increase pressure on ordinary people."[1]

items.title: Iran's 'mosquito fleet' holds Hormuz despite 155 warships sunk

featured_image.name: Why Iran has a speedboat swarm that's punching above its ...

items.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, U.S. and allied strikes have sunk more than 155 Iranian naval vessels and wiped out entire classes of warships. Yet the fleet Tehran relies on most to control the Strait of Hormuz — a sprawling armada of small, fast boats operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps — remains largely intact and continues to menace one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: China reaches 125 GW to become world's largest nuclear power

featured_image.name: Phase 1 of world's largest nuclear power base goes live in China

The milestone underscores Beijing's accelerating push to expand its atomic energy fleet at a pace unmatched by any other nation.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver

featured_image.name: Trump ups sanctions on Russian oil

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.[1][2]

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.[2]

items.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza
